title: Bottlenecks
hook: Hiring another salesperson won't help if production is the thing that's already maxed out.
statement: A system is only as strong as its tightest constraint.
explainer: Pushing harder on stages that already have room does nothing. Output is capped by the slowest stage. Widen that one and everything moves faster.
sop: Map your process and estimate each stage's capacity per day.
Find the minimum. That's your bottleneck.
Remove, automate, or delegate part of that stage's work.
Re-measure total output to confirm it went up.
Move on to the next slowest stage. There's always one.
equation_example: Intake 50 orders a day, Production 20, Shipping 45. Output is the minimum, 20 orders a day. Not the average. Raising the lowest number raises output. Raising a strong stage does nothing until the bottleneck moves.
question: Name the bottleneck you've put up with for months and one piece of it you could hand off.
closing_statement: The whole system moves at the bottleneck's pace.
